name: raylight
description: Cinematic product and launch videos, edited by your AI inside a live motion design editor.

interface.longDescription:
Raylight lets ChatGPT make and edit motion design videos for you: product videos, launch videos, and app demos, built in Raylight's browser editor with real 3D camera moves, device frames, lighting, typography, and sound. ChatGPT works inside your open Raylight project the way a motion designer would.

ChatGPT reads your project (shots, layers, colors, fonts, timing), makes edits in batches, then renders real frames of the result to check its own work and fix what reads wrong. Every change appears on your canvas as it happens and is undoable like your own edits. Hand it screenshots, logos, video clips, or audio and it places them; ask for a template and it starts from one of Raylight's official motion templates and swaps in your copy and media.

What people use it for: turning a few screenshots into a launch video, animating a headline and a push-in, scoring cuts with library sound, making an existing video match a brand, reviewing a shot and tightening its timing.

How it works: open your project at raylight.app, ask ChatGPT for a change, watch it happen. Edits and renders run through your open editor tab, so the tab stays open while ChatGPT works (it does not need to be visible). Exports and share links come from Raylight itself.

Requires a Raylight account, which you can create from the sign-in screen when you connect. Every tool and example prompts: raylight.app/mcp/docs.
capabilities: Read a project's shots, layers, colors, fonts, and timing
Edit layers, animation, camera moves, and sound in batches
Render real frames of a shot to check the result
Upload screenshots, logos, video, and audio into a project
Start a project from an official motion template
Check sound sync against the cuts
List exported videos and customize their share page
defaultPrompt: Turn these three screenshots into a 15 second launch video.
Make the headline slide up and add a slow push-in, then show me the first shot.
Start a new project from a Raylight template and put my logo in it.

positive.description: Start a project from a template
positive.prompt: List my Raylight templates and start a new project from the first one.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the template list, creates a project from the first one, and gives a link to open it in Raylight.

positive.prompt: Describe my open Raylight project shot by shot.
positive.expected_behavior: With the project open in a browser tab, summarizes each shot's layers, timing, and style.

positive.description: Edit and verify with a render
positive.prompt: Make the headline slide up over half a second and add a slow push-in, then render the first shot to check it.
positive.expected_behavior: Applies the edits (visible live in the editor tab, undoable there), renders frames of shot 1, and describes what it sees.

positive.prompt: Upload this image and put it in shot 2. (attach any PNG)
positive.expected_behavior: The image lands in the project's asset library and is placed as a layer in shot 2.

positive.prompt: Show me a filmstrip of the first shot and check whether the sound lines up with the cuts.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns a filmstrip, a waveform, and a sync report naming any hits that miss a cut.

negative.prompt: Describe my open Raylight project. (with every Raylight tab closed)
Open the Raylight project with id 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 and describe it.
Use Raylight to generate a photorealistic AI video of a person talking.

review.commerce_description: Raylight sells nothing inside ChatGPT. When a plan limit applies, the app states it and links an informational pricing page; there are no upgrade prompts, checkout links, or credit sales.

publication.release_notes: Initial release: read, edit, render, upload, templates, sound sync, and share page tools for Raylight projects.
